title: Catalogue Token Delivery
summary: Deliver Catalogue as the first semantic-token family, with combined discovery, immutable identity, tolerant projection, and broken-link repair.
content_html:
Catalogue Token Delivery

Complete Result

Deliver Catalogue as the first complete semantic-token family:

  • combined Work, Series, and Moment discovery;
  • accepted catalogue-token syntax and family/target data contracts;
  • Add catalogue token toolbar action and required-data modal;
  • caret recognition, exact-range highlighting, Catalogue Info view, update, and removal;
  • builder parsing and manage-only usage-index generation;
  • migration of the active Work occurrence into the Catalogue family;
  • semantic-token diagnosis and repair through the existing manage-only Docs Broken Links report.

This delivery proves that an author can begin with ambiguous text, compare different catalogue entity types, choose the best association, and then maintain the occurrence without changing its identity. It does not add Tag, asset, image, file, or another token family.

CT-P1 and CT-P2 are accepted after tactile review. Broken-link repair, migration, and pilot cleanup remain P3 and have not started.

Delivery Rule

Deliver the smallest complete vertical capability that replaces the existing Work token and leaves an additive path for later fields and token families. This delivery does not need to predict the final registry, every projection, or the next refactor.

Work, Series, and Moment share one minimal Catalogue lookup shape. The active 3 symbols Work occurrence is the migration and completion specimen. Richer type-specific fields are added only when a later UI or consumer requires them.

CT-P0 Scope And Impact

The versioned contract fixture at docs-viewer/tests/fixtures/semantic_tokens_catalogue_v1.json is the exact P0 authority. It records the grammar, Catalogue definition, resolved and broken specimens, ambiguous nerve discovery rows, and minimum lookup, usage, and broken-link shapes. The fixture is test input, not runtime configuration.

This checkpoint prevents Python/browser grammar drift and gives the later UI, builder, usage, and audit work one additive contract. The main risk is freezing syntax before tactile UI review; P1 therefore remains a separate review gate. There is no public, write-service, security, semantic-token generated-output, or production runtime change in P0. Routine Studio document and search projections may update from these source-document edits.

CT-P0 — Freeze The First Contract And Fixtures

Outcome: approve the exact source, UI, lookup, build, usage, and broken-link behavior for one resolved Work token and one broken Work token before production code changes.

  • [x] Accept the Source Editor UI and Architecture as the direction for this slice.
  • [x] Fix the exact Catalogue token syntax: delimiters, family, concrete target type, immutable id, Title, escaping, and deterministic serialization.
  • [x] Fix shared Python/browser fixtures for valid, escaped, malformed, code-context, adjacent-token, and caret-boundary cases.
  • [x] Use the existing 3 symbols Work 00638 occurrence as the resolved and migration fixture.
  • [x] Fix one deliberately absent Work identity as the broken fixture and record its exact raw source, unchanged rendered result, and Broken Links row.
  • [x] Retain nerve as the ambiguous discovery fixture: at minimum Work 00008 and Series 105 must be distinguishable in one result set.
  • [x] Accept the minimum token fields: family, target type, target id, and occurrence Title.
  • [x] Accept the minimum token-kind definition: key and labels, id policy, lookup adapter, declared lookup fields, and UI contribution ids.
  • [x] Accept the minimum target lookup row: family/type, id, title, workable href, and optional compact meta.
  • [x] Accept the minimum resolved usage row: source document/range, raw token, occurrence Title, target identity, and resolved href.
  • [x] Accept the minimum semantic broken-link row: source document/range, raw token, parsed identity where available, and failure reason.
  • [x] Name only the source-action, modal, Info-host, current-buffer, and guarded range refactors required by these fixtures.
  • [x] Prove the fixture and JSON shapes are versioned and additive; do not build an executable config/plugin framework.

Required later refactors are deliberately limited:

  • contribute source-add-catalogue-token without adding a Catalogue branch to generic source-editor lifecycle code;
  • keep the existing management modal shell and extract the pilot mixed-target search/list into the Catalogue-owned add-modal workflow;
  • replace the fixed semantic-token-picker Info default with contextual routing between ordinary source information and catalogue-token-info;
  • extend the source adapter with a current-buffer snapshot and monotonic local revision;
  • add exact-range selection and guarded replacement/removal that verify the expected raw token before mutation.

The fixture, its README entry, and test_semantic_tokens_catalogue_contract.py are the complete P0 fixture/test surface. Their versioned envelopes require minimum fields but permit additive fields. Removing or changing a required field, grammar rule, reason value, or meaning requires a new schema version.

P0 may add contract fixtures and focused conformance tests. It does not change production behavior. Stop for review after P0 and do not start P1 until the fixtures and minimal shapes are accepted.

P0 Evidence — 2026-07-26

  • Focused pytest: 5 passed. This checks fixture version/category coverage, definition fields, raw source ranges, deterministic serialized specimens, caret boundaries, minimum JSON fields, and resolved/broken specimen consistency. It does not execute a production parser, browser UI, builder resolver, usage generator, or Broken Links audit.
  • Explicit Python lint passed for docs-viewer/tests/python/test_semantic_tokens_catalogue_contract.py; it says nothing about unchanged Python or JavaScript.
  • Targeted Studio docs and search dry runs reported zero pending changes and zero docs warnings after the normal generated projection updated.
  • git diff --check passed.
  • Independent diff review found no runtime registry, production parser, UI, builder, report, public projection, compatibility alias, or generated semantic-token artifact in P0. It found no evidence that the current documentation or lint boundary needs a separate adoption change.

CT-P1 — Catalogue Creation UI

Outcome: an author can select or type text, search Catalogue in one modal, choose the concrete target, and insert the accepted token into the local source buffer.

  • [x] Add one Add catalogue token source-editor toolbar action.
  • [x] Extract the pilot title-weighted search and keyboard-navigable result list from its Info-panel host and place it in the Catalogue modal.
  • [x] Search Work, Series, and Moment together using the shared minimal lookup row; show type, id, title, and compact meta.
  • [x] Capture selection text and range before modal focus; use the text to seed search, prefill Title, and replace the captured range.
  • [x] Let the author compare and change results until confirming the concrete target type and id.
  • [x] Make modal confirmation the only semantic validation gate: require a current result, required Title, and successful serialization.
  • [x] Add only the generic action/modal/source-adapter contribution points required by this workflow; keep Catalogue knowledge outside core.
  • [x] Preserve local dirty state, focus return, cancellation, keyboard behavior, and the existing Rebuild ownership.

P1 review: manually review ambiguous nerve search, result distinction, selection prefilling, insertion, cancellation, keyboard use, modal fit, and narrow layout. Stop before P2 if the UI cannot express the P0 contract cleanly.

P1 Scope And Impact

The manage source editor now contributes source-add-catalogue-token through a generic main-view control handler and projects its enabled state through a generic source-action id list. The Catalogue-owned modal captures the source range before focus moves, adapts the existing generated Work, Series, and Moment lookup, validates a current result and required Title at confirmation, and guarded-replaces only the captured local range.

The lookup rows now carry the P0-required workable href. This remains the pilot semantic-references generated artifact until the accepted P2/P3 replacement and cleanup; P1 does not add a semantic-token registry, parser, builder projection, usage index, report, public payload, or write endpoint. The former manage-only Info-panel picker and its immediate select-to-insert composition are removed. Ordinary metadata information remains the source-mode Info-panel default until P2 adds caret-driven Catalogue information.

P1 Automated Evidence — 2026-07-26

  • Focused pytest: 7 passed across the P0 Catalogue contract and semantic target lookup generator. This proves fixture conformance and required generated href values for inspected synthetic Work, Series, and Moment rows; it does not prove P2 parsing, building, usage generation, or broken-link diagnosis.
  • The focused Catalogue browser-module smoke passed. It executes the browser serializer against every supported P0 fixture specimen and checks mixed nerve results, result distinction, keyboard choice, selection prefilling, current-result and required-Title validation, escaped insertion, caret insertion, cancellation, dirty-buffer mutation, stale captured-range rejection, the Search-to-results-to-Title tab-stop boundary, and active-result scrolling without horizontal result overflow. It also checks that click and Enter selection refresh Title, and loads the real modal/source-editor CSS to confirm that initial keyboard-modal focus before :focus-visible, first Tab, and subsequent arrow navigation do not restore an outer list border. It does not assess focus feel, narrow layout, screen-reader output, or a real canonical dataset.
  • The synthetic manage-route smoke passed with an isolated writable projects base. It checks that the action is registered, appears only in Markdown source mode, and dispatches to the accepted modal id without regressing the inspected manage shell. Its intercepted document/source payloads do not prove persistent repository-document writes or real target-data load timing.
  • Explicit lint passed for 13 changed JavaScript files and 4 changed Python files. This is named-file syntax/style evidence, not repository-wide lint.
  • The target lookup generator dry-run reported 2,130 rows and would write; the subsequent explicit write produced the same 2,130-row generated artifact.
  • Targeted Studio docs and search dry runs reported zero pending writes and zero docs warnings after the normal watcher projection. git diff --check passed.

P1 UI Review Gate — Accepted 2026-07-26

The live manage route review accepted ambiguous nerve comparison, visible target distinction, selection prefilling, insertion and cancellation feel, keyboard behavior, modal fit, and the narrow layout after the result-list focus and clipping corrections.

Individual result rows remain outside the tab order. The Results list is one tab stop between Search and Title; while it is focused, Up/Down moves and reveals the active result and Enter commits it. The list deliberately suppresses the shared modal focus border for every list focus state, not only :focus-visible; the moving active-row highlight carries the interaction state without clipped or doubled scroller edges. Border-box sizing still keeps result content within the scroller. Committing any result by click or Enter refreshes Title from that result; the author can then edit the occurrence Title. The modal confirmation label is Add. The source-toolbar action uses 📍 so the conventional link icon remains available for a future generic link action. This interaction is the accepted P1 baseline.

CT-P2 — Recognition, Info, And Tolerant Projection

Outcome: the inserted token can be recognized and maintained in source, and rebuild creates a link and usage relationship only when its lookup row supplies a workable destination.

  • [x] Add the accepted token-definition registry entries for catalogue:work, catalogue:series, and catalogue:moment.
  • [x] Generate the combined lookup with the P0 fields and accepted canonical adapters; do not expose raw canonical records or arrays.
  • [x] Implement aligned browser and Python parsing/serialization against the P0 fixtures.
  • [x] Detect a Catalogue token from the caret in the current unsaved buffer and select its exact source range.
  • [x] Show a Catalogue Info view with read-only family/type/id, editable Title, declared read-only title/link context, Update token, and Remove token.
  • [x] Keep target search and identity replacement out of the Info view; changing identity remains Remove followed by Add.
  • [x] Guard exact-range update/removal against stale buffer offsets.
  • [x] Resolve builder links through the target lookup rather than constructing a route from an id alone.
  • [x] Leave malformed, unsupported, unresolved, or destination-less strings unchanged; emit no semantic link, usage row, warning, or build failure.
  • [x] Generate by-document and by-target usage data only for resolved occurrences under the accepted semantic-tokens generated location.

P2 review: the resolved Work fixture inserts, activates, updates, removes, rebuilds to the accepted link, and appears in usage data. The broken fixture remains ordinary text and absent from usage data. Focused parser, range, registry, lookup, builder, and Info-view checks pass.

P2 Scope And Impact

The accepted registry and 2,130-row combined target lookup now live under semantic-tokens. The lookup exposes only family, concrete target type, canonical id, title, workable href, and compact meta; the document builder uses that lookup as its only link-resolution authority.

Python and browser parsers share the P0 grammar behavior, including exact zero-based half-open ranges and inactive code/comment contexts. In source mode, ordinary selections retain metadata information while a supported Catalogue occurrence routes to Catalogue Info and selects the exact current-buffer range. Update and removal both require the captured revision and raw source to remain unchanged.

Entering Markdown source automatically opens its configured Metadata Info view. Closing Info remains a direct user choice for the rest of that source session: caret movement does not reopen it, while leaving and re-entering source starts a new session and opens it again. Token recognition and exact-range selection remain owned by the mounted Catalogue Info contribution rather than generic source-editor core.

If the Add action captures one complete Catalogue token, the modal parses that structured input, displays its type-qualified id as the search query, restores only the exact family/type/id target, and preserves the occurrence Title. A missing exact identity produces a specific unavailable-target state with no Title fallback. Ordinary modal discovery remains fuzzy but now accepts bare ids and type-qualified ids as well as Titles.

Resolved occurrences render as links and produce deterministic index, by-document, and by-target usage envelopes under each local scope's semantic-tokens output. Public read-only scope builds leave the strings literal and produce no semantic-token usage directory or other semantic-token projection. Unsupported, malformed, missing, or destination-less targets remain literal source with no usage row or warning. The pilot registry, references, report wiring, and active Work occurrence remain untouched for P3.

Local manage-mode destinations keep their portable lookup href, but the Info view and rendered semantic-token anchors resolve that path against the environment-backed public-preview base. They therefore open the separate local site preview rather than the Docs Viewer service origin.

P2 Automated Evidence — 2026-07-26

  • Focused Python tests: 86 passed and 1 skipped across the P0/production parser, registry, lookup, builder, targeted/full rebuild, sub-scope, document-package, public-scope, static-asset, and Catalogue build-command surfaces. The document-package HTTP case skipped because local socket binding is unavailable in the sandbox. This is not repository-wide test coverage.
  • The focused Catalogue browser-module smoke passed. It executes every P0 parser/serializer specimen and caret boundary, ambiguous mixed-target search, bare and type-qualified id search, complete-token exact-identity restoration, occurrence-Title preservation, missing-identity rejection without fuzzy fallback, modal insertion, current-buffer exact-range activation, read-only target context, Title update, removal, stale-range rejection, and contextual metadata/Catalogue Info routing. It uses synthetic buffers and targets rather than persistent repository documents.
  • The shared router and metadata Info-view module smokes passed. The router smoke additionally proves that source entry opens the configured Metadata Info view, a manual close survives panel updates and rendered mode, and the next source entry opens it again. These checks protect the inspected hosted-view/coordinator seams, not the complete manage route or tactile panel behavior.
  • The Catalogue module smoke resolves both Info and rendered Work destinations through http://127.0.0.1:4000 while retaining the relative lookup row. The Docs Viewer service-config tests cover the SITE_PREVIEW_BASE override, default site host/port fallback, route-config projection, and invalid-base rejection.
  • Explicit lint passed for 13 changed JavaScript files and 15 changed Python files. This is named-file syntax/style evidence, not repository-wide lint.
  • The production target-lookup dry run reported 2,130 rows and unchanged after the explicit write.
  • Targeted Studio document and search dry runs reported zero pending writes and zero document warnings after the watcher projection.
  • The live manage route loaded the current source toolbar and discarded a temporary unsaved token without writing source. The in-app browser did not reliably move the textarea caret by one character, so exact live caret activation is not claimed here; the focused browser-module smoke is the evidence for that choreography.

P2 Review Gate — Accepted 2026-07-26

The live manage-route review accepted exact-range activation, contextual Info switching, target context, Title update and removal, local-preview destinations, source-entry Info opening with direct manual close, and exact-identity restoration when Add captures a complete token. Redundant success-status messages were removed. A broader Info-panel visual redesign, including a top-row icon toolbar, is deferred to its own later slice.

CT-P2 is closed. CT-P3 remains unstarted.

CT-P3 — Broken-Link Repair, Migration, And Cleanup

Outcome: unresolved semantic-token links have a practical repair path, the active Work token uses the new contract, and the pilot wiring is gone.

  • [ ] Extend the existing Docs Broken Links audit and report with the P0 semantic-token broken-link row; add no separate Semantic Tokens report.
  • [ ] Scan source independently of the resolved usage index and report unsupported kind, missing target, and missing workable destination.
  • [ ] Open the owning document in source mode from a report row. Select the exact occurrence only if the P0 handoff can support it without a broader editor refactor.
  • [ ] Keep repair user-controlled: fix canonical/projection data where appropriate, or Remove the source token and Add the correct target through the validated modal.
  • [ ] Migrate the active 3 symbols Work occurrence without changing its target or displayed Title.
  • [ ] Rebuild lookup and usage output rather than migrating generated JSON record by record.
  • [ ] Remove pilot names, paths, registry shape, Info-panel picker placement, route-only unresolved linking, report wiring, and public relationship copies after their replacements are active.
  • [ ] Add no compatibility aliases or public replacement.

P3 review: the broken fixture appears in Docs Broken Links with source and reason but does not block rebuild; its repair clears the audit. The migrated 3 symbols occurrence renders and indexes correctly. Focused report, route, module, and migration checks plus the targeted Docs build and git diff --check pass.

Explicitly Deferred

  • Series context on a Work occurrence;
  • preview images and other richer lookup presentation;
  • media, file, or download projections and canonical array handling;
  • occurrence fields beyond Title or a general field-control system;
  • type-specific metadata beyond the shared minimal Catalogue lookup row;
  • Tag, asset, image, file, or another token family;
  • canonical Work, Series, or Moment editing;
  • a standalone Semantic Tokens report, route, service, or validation system;
  • public semantic relationships, related-content UI, or focused public payloads;
  • automatic conversion or semantic wrapping of ordinary Markdown links or media;
  • a general plugin architecture or compatibility layer for a possible future refactor.
